title: The Sultan's Blessing for Kagōunga
description: Kagōunga was honored to be invited by the Sultan of Ternate: appreciation for Popeda Instant, a path to the Maluku diaspora, and a blessing for the Kagōunga name.
excerpt: Kagōunga was honored to be invited by the Sultan of Ternate, receiving appreciation for Popeda Instant and a blessing for the Kagōunga name.
lede: Ternate, January 10, 2025 — Kagōunga was honored to be invited by the Sultan of Ternate, Sultan Hidayatullah Syah, to the Kedaton of the Sultanate of Ternate.
bodyMarkdown:
The meeting on January 10, 2025, marked an important moment in Kagōunga's journey. For an innovation born in Ternate that brings popeda forward as part of North Maluku's culinary identity, meeting the Sultan was more than an opportunity to introduce a product. It was also an opportunity to receive recognition and support from a cultural institution deeply connected to the history and identity of Ternate.

During the occasion, Sultan Hidayatullah Syah expressed his appreciation for Kagōunga's effort to present popeda in a more practical format through Popeda Instant. The Sultan then asked for the product to be prepared and served directly. The moment reflected Kagōunga's commitment to preserving the character and experience of popeda while presenting it in a modern and accessible format.

The Sultan's support also opened a new opportunity for Kagōunga's journey. He expressed his intention to help create a pathway for the product to reach the Maluku diaspora in the Netherlands. For Kagōunga, this opportunity represents more than market expansion. The Maluku diaspora in the Netherlands is part of a long history connecting the Maluku Islands with the wider world. Bringing the taste of popeda back to this community is therefore also a way of reconnecting people with the flavors and stories of their homeland.

The name **Kagōunga** itself is directly connected to the history of the Sultanate of Ternate. It is derived from **Kagunga**, the great vessel of the Sultanate, which represents the grandeur and maritime heritage of the Ternate Sultanate. The use of the name received the blessing of Sultan Hidayatullah Syah.

That blessing has become an important part of Kagōunga's identity. The name represents more than a brand. It serves as a reminder that Kagōunga's innovation is rooted in the cultural heritage of Ternate and North Maluku.

Through Popeda Instant as one of its signature products, Kagōunga carries the belief that culinary heritage does not have to remain confined to the past. By honoring its ingredients, flavors, and stories of origin, heritage can be transformed into products that live within modern life while reaching Maluku communities across the world.

From the Kedaton of the Sultanate of Ternate on January 10, 2025, Kagōunga entered a new chapter: carrying popeda from its homeland into a wider world, with the Sultan's blessing and a vision to bring the flavors and identity of the Spice Islands to the global stage.

title: Kagōunga at Ubud Food Festival 2026
description: Kagōunga introduced North Maluku cuisine to national and international audiences at Ubud Food Festival 2026, from Masterclass to food stall collaborations.
excerpt: Kagōunga introduced North Maluku cuisine to national and international audiences at Ubud Food Festival 2026, from Masterclass to food stall collaborations.
lede: Ubud, Bali, May 31, 2026 — Kagōunga was invited to participate in the Ubud Food Festival (UFF) 2026, held from May 28–31, 2026, in Ubud, Bali.
bodyMarkdown:
As part of the *Masterclass* at Mana Earthly Paradise, Ubud, Kagōunga presented an authentic selection of North Maluku dishes to an exclusive audience, including *Popeda with Turmeric Fish Soup, Nutmeg Lemonade, Sarabati, Sinyole,* and *Sambal Roa*. The presentation introduced participants to the flavors, techniques, and stories behind Ternate’s culinary traditions.

Kagōunga’s participation also included collaborations with *Javara Indigenous Indonesia* and *Seniman Pangan*. These collaborations brought together local food knowledge, indigenous Indonesian ingredients, and contemporary gastronomic approaches, creating a wider platform for North Maluku cuisine within Indonesia’s evolving culinary landscape.

Throughout UFF 2026, Kagōunga was entrusted to appear across *four different segments, including **Masterclass, Food Stall by Javara, and Fast Forward*, alongside other festival programs that connected Kagōunga with gastronomic professionals, chefs, media, and audiences from diverse backgrounds.

The participation generated significant exposure for Kagōunga while bringing greater attention to the culinary heritage of North Maluku and Ternate. Popeda, nutmeg, sarabati, sinyole, and sambal roa became gateways to introduce the region’s ingredients, traditions, and culinary identity to a wider audience.

*Janet DeNeefe*, Founder of Ubud Food Festival, also expressed strong appreciation for Kagōunga’s presentation. Her recognition further affirmed Kagōunga’s position as a representative of Eastern Indonesian cuisine, demonstrating how local culinary heritage can be presented on a contemporary gastronomic stage while retaining its distinctive character.

Kagōunga’s participation in UFF 2026 marks an important milestone in its mission to introduce North Maluku culture through gastronomy. From Ternate to Ubud, Kagōunga brought more than food. It brought stories, ingredients, traditions, and the identity of the Spice Islands to a wider world.

title: Kagōunga at Kunstkring Dialogue 2026
description: Kagōunga joined national changemakers at Kunstkring Dialogue 2026 in Jakarta, bringing the spirit of Move, Moreover into conversations on restorative economy.
excerpt: Kagōunga joined national changemakers at Kunstkring Dialogue 2026 in Jakarta, bringing the spirit of Move, Moreover into conversations on restorative economy.
lede: Jakarta, June 26, 2026 — Kagōunga was invited to participate in Kunstkring Dialogue 2026, held from June 24–26, 2026, at Tugu Kunstkring, Jakarta.
bodyMarkdown:
At the forum, Kagōunga joined a distinguished group of figures and changemakers, including *Veronica Tan, Deputy Minister of Women’s Empowerment and Child Protection; Irine Umar, Deputy Minister of Creative Economy; Sherly Tjoanda, Governor of North Maluku;* and *Monica Tanuhandaru, Founder of Bamboo Foundation*.

Kagōunga also participated alongside journalists and media figures *Rosiana Silalahi* and *Desi Anwar*, as well as weavers and bamboo artisans from Wogo Village, Flores, East Nusa Tenggara. The cross-sector gathering provided a platform for exchanging ideas on culture, creativity, economy, environment, and sustainability.

The Kunstkring Dialogue 2026 was broadcast live by *CNN Indonesia* and *Kompas TV, generating broad national exposure for Kagōunga. The occasion also introduced the spirit of **Move, Moreover* as part of Kagōunga’s ongoing cultural diplomacy mission for North Maluku through food, art, creativity, and innovation.

For Kagōunga, the concept of a restorative economy is closely connected to its approach to cultural heritage. Sustainability is not only about economic growth, but also about preserving ancestral knowledge, ecosystems, food resources, and the foundations of life for generations to come.

*Aiya Lee, Co-Founder of Kagōunga*, said that Kunstkring Dialogue 2026 strongly aligned with Kagōunga’s commitment to preserving ancestral heritage, including the earth and all forms of life it sustains. For Kagōunga, preserving heritage means ensuring that these values remain alive and relevant for future generations.

Kagōunga’s participation in Kunstkring Dialogue 2026 marks another step in expanding the cultural diplomacy of North Maluku. Through the spirit of *Move, Moreover*, Kagōunga brings the perspectives of Ternate and the Spice Islands into national conversations while demonstrating how local heritage can contribute to a more sustainable future.
